ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $AB$ and $CD$ are diameters of $\odot O$, with chords $DE$ and $BF$ intersecting the radii $AO$ and $CO$ at points $G$ and $H$, respectively, and $\angle FBA=\angle EDC$. Given $DE=BF$, and if $\overset{\frown}{AE}=\overset{\frown}{EF}=\overset{\frown}{FC}$, and $\angle DOB=\angle EGO$, what is the degree measure of $\overset{\frown}{AC}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, since $OB = OD$, it follows that $\angle 1 = \angle 2$, therefore $\angle DOB = 180^\circ - 2\angle 1$. Since $\angle EGO = \angle EDB + \angle ABD = \angle 3 + \angle 1 + \angle 2 = \angle 3 + 2\angle 1$, and $\angle DOB = \angle EGO$, it follows that $180^\circ - 2\angle 1 = \angle 3 + 2\angle 1$, therefore $\angle 3 = 180^\circ - 4\angle 1$. Since $\overset{\frown}{AE} = \overset{\frown}{EF} = \overset{\frown}{FC}$, it follows that $\angle 3 = 2\angle ADE$, therefore $\angle ADE = \frac{1}{2}\angle 3$. Since $CD$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, it follows that $\overset{\frown}{AD} + \overset{\frown}{AE} + \overset{\frown}{CE} = 180^\circ$, therefore $\angle 2 + \angle ADE + \angle 3 = 90^\circ$, hence $\angle 1 + \frac{1}{2} \times (180^\circ - 4\angle 1) + (180^\circ - 4\angle 1) = 90^\circ$, therefore $5\angle 1 = 180^\circ$, thus $\angle 1 = 36^\circ$, hence $\angle DOB = 180^\circ - 36^\circ \times 2 = 108^\circ$, therefore $\angle AOC = 108^\circ$, hence the degree of $\overset{\frown}{AC}$ is $\boxed{108^\circ}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, $AB$ and $CD$ are diameters of $\odot O$, with chords $DE$ and $BF$ intersecting the radii $AO$ and $CO$ at points $G$ and $H$, respectively, and $\angle FBA=\angle EDC$. Given $DE=BF$, and if $\overset{\frown}{AE}=\overset{\frown}{EF}=\overset{\frown}{FC}$, and $\angle DOB=\angle EGO$, what is the degree measure of $\overset{\frown}{AC}$?
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, since $OB = OD$, it follows that $\angle 1 = \angle 2$, therefore $\angle DOB = 180^\circ - 2\angle 1$. Since $\angle EGO = \angle EDB + \angle ABD = \angle 3 + \angle 1 + \angle 2 = \angle 3 + 2\angle 1$, and $\angle DOB = \angle EGO$, it follows that $180^\circ - 2\angle 1 = \angle 3 + 2\angle 1$, therefore $\angle 3 = 180^\circ - 4\angle 1$. Since $\overset{\frown}{AE} = \overset{\frown}{EF} = \overset{\frown}{FC}$, it follows that $\angle 3 = 2\angle ADE$, therefore $\angle ADE = \frac{1}{2}\angle 3$. Since $CD$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, it follows that $\overset{\frown}{AD} + \overset{\frown}{AE} + \overset{\frown}{CE} = 180^\circ$, therefore $\angle 2 + \angle ADE + \angle 3 = 90^\circ$, hence $\angle 1 + \frac{1}{2} \times (180^\circ - 4\angle 1) + (180^\circ - 4\angle 1) = 90^\circ$, therefore $5\angle 1 = 180^\circ$, thus $\angle 1 = 36^\circ$, hence $\angle DOB = 180^\circ - 36^\circ \times 2 = 108^\circ$, therefore $\angle AOC = 108^\circ$, hence the degree of $\overset{\frown}{AC}$ is $\boxed{108^\circ}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is circle O; both AB and CD pass through the center O, so they are two intersecting diameters; A is on the upper-left side, B is on the lower-right side, D is on the lower-left side, and C is on the upper-right side. Chord DE is on the left side and intersects radius AO at G, so ∠EGO is formed by DE and the line where diameter AB lies; chord BF is on the right side and intersects radius CO at H. Points A, E, F, C are successively located on the upper arc. Reasoning: Let x=∠ABD. Because A, O, B are collinear, C, O, D are collinear, and OB=OD, triangle OBD is an isosceles triangle, giving ∠ABD=∠BDO=x, therefore ∠DOB=180°−2x. Also let y=∠EDC, namely the small angle at D in the figure formed by DE and DC. Because ∠EDB=∠EDC+∠CDB=y+x, and ∠DBA=x, so ∠EGO=∠EDB+∠DBA=(y+x)+x=y+2x. The problem gives ∠DOB=∠EGO, thus 180°−2x=y+2x, giving y=180°−4x. Also because arc AE=arc EF=arc FC, what ∠EDC subtends is arc EC=arc EF+arc FC, while what ∠ADE subtends is arc AE, so y=2∠ADE, namely ∠ADE=y/2. Since CD is a diameter, the semicircular arc passing through D, A, E, F, C is 180°; adding the corresponding inscribed angles gives x+∠ADE+y=90°. Substituting ∠ADE=y/2 and y=180°−4x gives x+(180°−4x)/2+(180°−4x)=90°, simplifying to 270°−5x=90°, so x=36°. Therefore ∠DOB=180°−2×36°=108°. AB and CD are intersecting diameters, so ∠AOC and ∠DOB are vertical angles, ∠AOC=108°, hence the measure of arc AC is 108°.
